titles: The Lone Accuser at the Gate
frames: {w} brings a capital charge of {@charge} against {d}, a business rival. {@wit}
At the gate of {town}, {d} stands accused of {@charge}. {@wit}

options.text: blasphemy
bowing down to another god
{w} swears earnestly that he saw and heard it himself, but no second witness can be produced.
{w} says he heard of it from two market gossips who will not come forward.
Two independent eyewitnesses, {w} and {w2}, each saw it themselves and agree on every detail.

hint: Before asking what the penalty is, ask whether the court has the proof the Torah demands.

stone.label: Sentence {d} to Stoning
stone.summary: Convict on the testimony and carry out the capital sentence, with the witnesses throwing first.

acquit.label: Bar Conviction & Acquit {d}
acquit.summary: Refuse capital or corporal punishment because the proof is legally insufficient.

half.label: Inflict Half-Penalty (20 Stripes)
half.summary: Impose moderate stripes on suspicion to deter future impiety.

jail.label: Imprison {d} Indefinitely
jail.summary: Hold the accused in confinement until a second witness appears.

oath.label: Sentence on {w}'s Sworn Oath
oath.summary: Accept the accuser's solemn oath as proof sufficient for execution.

rules.rationale: With two independent eyewitnesses the evidentiary threshold is met (Deut 17:6), and the capital sentence stands, carried out with the witnesses throwing first (Deut 17:7).

blessing.title: Proof Properly Weighed
blessing.effect: The guilty are held to account, and the people trust that proof matters.

rules.rationale: Mosaic jurisprudence strictly requires at least two direct eyewitnesses for conviction (Num 35:30; Deut 17:6; 19:15). A lone accuser or hearsay can never justify execution, punishment on suspicion, or indefinite detention.

blessing.title: Evidentiary Integrity Upheld
blessing.effect: Citizens trust the court's impartiality; malicious accusations fail at the threshold.

frames: During a trial at {town}, close questioning by the judges exposes that {w1} and {w2} conspired to fabricate testimony {@plot}.
{d} stands accused at {town}, but the judges' cross-examination breaks {w1} and {w2}: they admit they lied {@plot}.

options.text: so that {d}, an innocent landholder, would be executed and his ancestral vineyard seized
so that {d} would be forced to pay {amt} shekels he did not owe
options.ev: the plotted punishment was a fine of {amt} shekels

options.text: so that {d} would be flogged for an offence he never committed

hint: What was the false witnesses' aim? The Torah turns their plan back on them.

death.label: Inflict the Plotted Death Penalty on the Witnesses
death.summary: Apply Lex Talionis: do to the false witnesses what they meant to do to {d}.

pay.label: Make the Witnesses Pay the Sum They Plotted
pay.summary: Order {w1} and {w2} to pay {amt} shekels to {d}.

lashes.label: Give the False Witnesses the Same Stripes
lashes.summary: Administer the flogging they meant {d} to suffer.

double.label: Fine Double and Release Them
double.summary: Assess a civil penalty on the conspirators and let them go.

rebuke.label: Exhort Them to Repentance
rebuke.summary: Dismiss the case with a stern priestly rebuke since no punishment was carried out.

rules.rationale: Under Deut 19:19 false witnesses receive the exact punishment they plotted against the accused. In a capital trial, that is death. This strict symmetry deters judicial murder.

blessing.title: Fear of Perjury Purged
blessing.effect: Conspirators see that weaponising the courts rebounds upon themselves; the innocent rest secure.

rules.rationale: The same measure applies: 'you shall do to him as he meant to do to his brother' (Deut 19:19). A plot to extract money is answered by making the plotters pay that money.

blessing.title: The Scheme Backfires
blessing.effect: Would-be extortionists learn that false testimony costs them what they sought.

rules.rationale: The punishment the witnesses sought is the punishment they receive (Deut 19:19), so a plot to have a man flogged is answered with the same flogging (capped under Deut 25:3).

blessing.title: A Mirror Held Up
blessing.effect: False witnesses suffer exactly what they intended for the innocent.

frames: At {town}, {d} has been tried for {@offence}. {@verdict} The younger judge, {j}, urges {n} stripes.
{d} had been tried at {town} for {@offence}. {@verdict} {j}, a judge, argues that {n} stripes would be fitting.

options.text: striking a neighbour in a quarrel
damaging a neighbour's irrigation channel
reviling an elder at the gate
Two witnesses proved the offence and the court has found that he deserves a beating.
The evidence cleared {d} completely, yet {j} wants a few stripes 'to be safe'.

hint: Check the verdict first, then recall the legal limit on beatings.

cap.label: Cap the Beating at Forty Stripes
cap.summary: Order no more than forty stripes, so {d} is not degraded.

asked.label: Order the {n} Stripes Requested
asked.summary: Follow {j}'s view and flog {d} until {n} have been given.

fine.label: Replace the Beating with a Fine
fine.summary: Waive stripes and take a fine to the elders in place of the beating.

acquit.label: Acquit {d} and Inflict Nothing
acquit.summary: The accused was proven innocent; no beating may follow.

rules.rationale: Judges must 'acquit the innocent' (Deut 25:1). A man cleared by the evidence may not be beaten on suspicion.

blessing.title: The Innocent Protected
blessing.effect: Citizens know a cleared man walks free.

rules.rationale: A guilty man who deserves a beating may receive at most forty stripes (Deut 25:2–3), so that he is not degraded before the community.

blessing.title: Punishment With Limits
blessing.effect: The court shows that even offenders keep their dignity.

frames: At {town}, {r}, a wealthy landowner, and {p}, a poor man, dispute a field. {@evidence} {@pull}
{r}, a wealthy landowner, and {p}, a poor man, come before the elders at {town} over a field. {@evidence} {@pull}
witness: A Dispute Between Rich and Poor

options.text: The boundary stones and two witnesses show the field belongs to {p}.
The boundary stones and two witnesses show the field belongs to {r}.
Before the hearing, {r} sends a gift of {amt} shekels to your house.
options.ev: gift offered by the rich party

options.text: {r} is the most respected man in the district, and no one wants to offend him.
options.ev: pressure to favour the great man

options.text: The whole gate pities {p}, a widow's son, and urges you to rule for him whatever the facts.
options.ev: public pressure to favour the poor man

hint: Set aside the gift, the reputation and the pity. What do the stones and the witnesses say?

split.label: Split the Field Between Them
split.summary: Divide the land equally to keep the peace.

adjourn.label: Adjourn Until Feelings Cool
adjourn.summary: Delay the case until the pressure on the gate has passed.

rules.rationale: 'You shall not accept a bribe' (Exod 23:8) and 'you shall not be partial to the great' (Lev 19:15). The judge follows the evidence, and here it supports the poor man.

blessing.title: The Bench Is Not for Sale
blessing.effect: The poor trust the court, and the rich learn silver cannot buy a ruling.

rules.rationale: 'You shall not be partial to a poor man in his dispute' (Exod 23:3) or show favouritism out of pity (Lev 19:15). The evidence supports the landowner, so the court rules for him.

blessing.title: Even-Handed Justice
blessing.effect: The court is trusted by rich and poor alike because pity does not decide cases.

frames: At {town}, the elders find that {m} used {@fraud} to cheat {v}, {@victim}. {@hurt} {m} argues that {v} does not merit the same remedy as a native-born Israelite.
{v}, {@victim}, accuses the merchant {m}, who used {@fraud}. {@hurt} {m} claims {v} is not entitled to full restitution.

options.text: rigged stone weights when selling grain
an undersized measuring jar when selling oil
a false balance when weighing silver
a resident alien (ger)
a poor foreign day-labourer living among the tribes
When confronted, {m} also struck {v}, leaving him bruised and out of work for three days.
{m} did nothing further, and {v} suffered no injury.

hint: The Torah has one standard for native and alien alike. Check whether anything beyond the fraud itself needs repaying.

full.label: Apply the Same Law: Restitution & Seize the Weights
full.summary: Give {v} full restoration of what was taken and destroy the false measure.

wages.label: Apply the Same Law: Restitution, Lost Wages & Seizure
wages.summary: Give {v} full restoration, pay for his lost time and healing, and destroy the false measure.

half.label: Award Half-Compensation Due to Status
half.summary: Apply reduced penalties as under neighbouring class-based codes.

dismiss.label: Dismiss: Strangers Have No Standing
dismiss.summary: Restrict Mosaic civil protections to native-born Israelites.

stripes.label: Administer 45 Stripes Without Compensation
stripes.summary: Flog the merchant beyond the forty-stripe cap and award {v} nothing.

rules.rationale: Leviticus 24:22 mandates one identical standard of law for the foreign resident and the native-born. Honest weights (Lev 19:35–36) and lost-time injury pay (Exod 21:18–19) apply in full.

blessing.title: One Law for All
blessing.effect: Foreigners trust the tribes' courts, and honest trade thrives.

rules.rationale: Leviticus 24:22 gives the resident alien the same law as the native-born, and false weights are an abomination (Lev 19:35–36; Deut 25:13–16). With no injury, full restitution and destruction of the measure complete the remedy.

blessing.title: Fair Trade Restored
blessing.effect: Merchants know a cheat answers to the same court whoever he cheats.

frames: At {town}, {w}, {@worker}, complains that {e} {@delay}. {e} says he will settle 'when it suits him'.

options.text: a poor day-labourer of the town
a poor resident alien who hires himself out
a poor hired shepherd
kept his day's wage overnight and refuses to pay it before morning
has withheld his pay for a full week
deducted a third of the wage, claiming {w:he} 'owes goodwill'

hint: How does the Torah treat a poor labourer's wage, and when is it due?

pay.label: Order the Full Wage Paid Before Sunset
pay.summary: Require {e} to pay in full on the same day, since the labourer depends on it.

month.label: Let the Employer Pay at Month's End
month.summary: Allow {e} to settle with all of his workers together at the end of the month, as suits him.

deduct.label: Allow the Employer's Deduction
deduct.summary: Let {e} keep the sum he says is owed to him in goodwill and pay only the balance.

fine.label: Fine the Employer and Leave the Wage Unpaid
fine.summary: Take a fine for the elders from {e} but make no order that the wage itself be paid.

rules.rationale: 'You shall not keep the wages of a hired worker with you all night until the morning' (Lev 19:13). A poor man's wage is due the same day, before the sun sets, whether he is a countryman or an alien (Deut 24:14–15).

blessing.title: The Poor Man Fed
blessing.effect: Labourers are paid on the day they earn, and the cry of the poor does not reach heaven against the gate.

frames: At {town}, {c} sues for {amt} shekels of interest on a loan to {b}, {@borrower}. {c} says the contract plainly allows it.
{b}, {@borrower}, borrowed silver from {c} and now refuses to pay the {amt} shekels of interest. {c} appeals to the contract.

options.text: a poor neighbour who borrowed grain to feed his family
a poor resident alien who borrowed to survive the winter
options.w: Loan to a Poor Resident Alien

options.text: a foreign merchant passing through who borrowed to buy trade goods

hint: Who is the borrower, and what is the loan for? The Torah does not treat every loan alike.

none.label: Strike the Interest; Principal Only
none.summary: Order {b} to repay the principal and cancel any interest.

ok.label: Permit the Agreed Interest
ok.summary: Enforce the contract exactly as written, with the interest included in the sum owed.

double.label: Award Double Interest as a Penalty
double.summary: Penalise {b} for the delay by awarding twice the interest named in the contract.

cancel.label: Cancel the Debt Entirely
cancel.summary: Forgive both the principal and the interest and declare the debt wiped out.

rules.rationale: The Torah permits interest on loans to a foreigner (nokhri) engaged in trade (Deut 23:20). The ban on interest protects the needy, not commercial borrowers from abroad.

blessing.title: Commerce Respected
blessing.effect: Trade with foreign merchants continues on clear terms.

rules.rationale: No interest may be charged to a poor countryman (Exod 22:25) or to a resident alien in need (Lev 25:35–37). A loan to the needy is covenant kindness, not a business.

blessing.title: Kindness Protected
blessing.effect: The poor can borrow without being crushed by interest.

frames: At {town}, {b} complains about {c}, who {@pledge}. {c} says the debt is real and the pledge is his right.
{c} defends himself before the elders of {town}: he {@pledge}, since {b} owes him money.

options.text: took {b}'s only cloak as a pledge and keeps it overnight
options.ev: poor man's only cloak held overnight

options.text: seized the upper millstone of {b}'s hand-mill as security
took a widow's garment as a pledge for her debt
barged into {b}'s house to pick out whatever he fancied as a pledge

hint: The Torah sets limits on what a creditor may take, when he must give it back, and how he may collect.

sunset.label: Return the Cloak Before Sunset
sunset.summary: Require the creditor to hand it back by nightfall so the poor man can sleep in it.

forbid.label: Forbid Taking It as a Pledge at All
forbid.summary: Order the item returned; it is a livelihood or a protected person's garment.

outside.label: Creditor Waits Outside; Debtor Brings It Out
outside.summary: Forbid entering the home and let the debtor choose what to hand over.

keep.label: Let the Creditor Hold It Until Repaid
keep.summary: Enforce the pledge as agreed for as long as the debt lasts.

forfeit.label: Forfeit the Item to the Creditor
forfeit.summary: Give the item to the creditor outright as payment.

rules.rationale: A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before the sun goes down, because it is the poor man's only covering (Exod 22:26–27; Deut 24:12–13).

blessing.title: A Warm Night for the Poor
blessing.effect: Creditors learn not to take what a man needs to live.

rules.rationale: A mill or upper millstone may not be taken in pledge (Deut 24:6), and neither may a widow's garment (Deut 24:17), since these take away a person's livelihood or protection.

blessing.title: Livelihoods Protected
blessing.effect: Creditors cannot strip the poor of their means of living.

rules.rationale: The creditor must stay outside, and the debtor brings the pledge out to him (Deut 24:10–11), preserving the dignity and privacy of the home.

blessing.title: A Man's House Is His Own
blessing.effect: Debtors keep their dignity even when they owe.
